subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should OpenClaw expose arbitrary caller-selected `sessions_spawn` lanes with per-lane configuration, or standardize bounded owner-derived isolation such as per-agent or per-parent lanes?
rationale: The missing capability is proven, but lane naming authority and configuration semantics are permanent model-facing and operator-facing contracts that overlap other open concurrency proposals and cannot be selected safely from source behavior alone.

options.title: Bounded owner lanes
options.body: Use per-agent or per-parent derived lanes with bounded capacity, retaining the current global lane as the compatibility default.

options.title: Caller-named lanes
options.body: Expose a validated arbitrary `sessions_spawn.lane` value and an explicit per-lane concurrency map for advanced orchestration.

options.title: Fair single pool
options.body: Retain one global sub-agent pool and address starvation through per-owner caps, fair scheduling, and queue visibility.

recommendation.title: Bounded owner lanes
recommendation.body: Use per-agent or per-parent derived lanes with bounded capacity, retaining the current global lane as the compatibility default.

likelyOwner.reason: The original feature commits and current blamed implementation most strongly connect steipete to both spawn dispatch paths and the global concurrency contract.
